steps.title: In the ground
steps.text: The seventeen rare earths always occur together, never alone. The light ones, gadolinium among them, come mainly from bastnäsite, mined in hard rock at Bayan Obo in China and Mountain Pass in California, and from monazite, a heavy grain in beach sands. Gadolinium is a minor part of bastnäsite and monazite, and richer in the southern Chinese clays.
steps.india: Monazite in the beach sands of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. It is rich in the light rare earths and poor in the heavy ones.

steps.title: Mine
steps.text: Bastnäsite is mined from open pits, crushed and floated to a concentrate of about 60% rare-earth oxide. Monazite is sorted out of dredged beach sand with magnets and electrostatic plates, alongside ilmenite and zircon.
steps.india: 2,900 tonnes of rare-earth oxide in 2025, 0.7% of the world, all from monazite in beach sands worked by IREL.

steps.title: Crack
steps.text: The concentrate is broken down with hot acid or caustic soda so the rare earths dissolve. Monazite also releases thorium and a little uranium, which are radioactive and must be removed and stored. What is left is a mixed rare-earth chloride or carbonate: all the elements still together.

steps.title: Separate
steps.text: This is the hard part. Neighbouring rare earths behave almost identically, so the solution is run through hundreds of solvent-extraction stages, each shifting the balance slightly, until gadolinium comes out on its own as an oxide. China does about 91% of the world's separation.
steps.india: IREL makes gadolinium oxide and has made 50 kg of 99.99% nuclear-grade oxide.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: For medicine, very pure gadolinium oxide is dissolved and locked inside an organic molecule, a chelate, which makes it safe to inject. For reactors the oxide is blended into uranium fuel pellets.
steps.india: A large generic-drug industry could make the chelates.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Gadolinium chelates are the contrast agents that make tumours and blood vessels show up in MRI scans. Gadolinium also absorbs neutrons better than any other stable element, which is why it is used to control nuclear fuel.
steps.india: Demand comes from hospitals and nuclear programmes.

steps.title: Recycle
steps.text: Very little is recovered from old products: each one holds grams, spread thin and hard to collect. Scrap from the factories that make these materials is the main source.
